messages.subject: Hurdle model
parts:
Dear all,

I am working on analyzing the spatial distribution of fish catch rate. There are many zeros in the dataset, so I developed a hurdle model, like the rainfall problem in The R-INLA tutorial on SPDE models. The first component is catch occurrence, and the second one is the catch amount (is NA when catch = 0). 

I have two questions here:
1. Is it appropriate to use this hurdle model to analyze fish catch problem? 
2. I can get two spatial distributions for catch occurrence and catch amount, respectively. How can I get a spatial distribution for catch rate (including the positive catch amount and zero catch)? Add them together?

The tutorial doesn't provide enough guidance on these points. I appreciate your help.

Thanks,
Ruby

The first component is catch occurrence, and the second one is the catch amount (is NA when catch = 0). 

I have two questions here:
1. Is it appropriate to use this hurdle model to analyze fish catch problem?
I think that it is at least useful.

2. I can get two spatial distributions for catch occurrence and catch amount, respectively. How can I get a spatial distribution for catch rate (including the positive catch amount and zero catch)? Add them together?

My colleague and I used a model for the probability and positives in some work and we considered samples from the posterior. That is we have samples for the probabilities and catch amount. It was considered jointly to compute the catch rate.

Elias

The tutorial doesn't provide enough guidance on these points. I appreciate your help.

Thanks,
Ruby

Dear Ruby,

 I'd recommend this excellent paper by Ali Arab on using hurdle models in INLA.

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4586626/

The sample code given in the article's supplement is fairly straightforward to follow.

Paul
